steps.text: On Thursday: Remove the turkey from the brine, discard the brine, and pat the turkey thoroughly dry with paper towels.
Let the turkey sit at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Mash 6 tablespoons softened butter with 3 minced garlic cloves and 1 teaspoon black pepper; loosen the skin over the breast and thighs and push 4 sage sprigs and 2 rosemary sprigs under the skin.

Rub the herb butter all over the outside of the bird; drizzle 2 tablespoons olive oil over the skin; stuff the cavity with 3 halved garlic cloves, 1 halved lemon, 1 quartered onion, and 4 thyme sprigs.

Scatter 3 celery stalks and 2 carrots (cut into large pieces) in the bottom of a large roasting pan; set the turkey breast-side up on a roasting rack over the vegetables and pour 2 cups chicken broth into the pan.
Roast the turkey at 325°F for about 2¾ hours; baste with pan drippings every 45 minutes.
Raise the oven to 350°F and put in the Sage and Onion Stuffing and Green Bean Casserole.
Keep roasting the turkey at 350°F for about 25 more minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F.
Transfer the turkey to a carving board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 20–30 minutes before carving; reserve the pan drippings for the gravy.
Carve the turkey and arrange on a large platter.
Serve the Herb-Roasted Whole Turkey with the Pan Gravy, Sage and Onion Stuffing, Mashed Potatoes, Cranberry-Orange Sauce, Green Bean Casserole and Sweet Potato Casserole.

On Thursday: pour the turkey drippings from the roasting pan into a fat separator or large measuring cup; skim off and reserve ½ cup fat (supplement with 4 tablespoons butter if needed), leaving the dark juices behind.
Set the roasting pan over two burners on medium-high; add the reserved fat and whisk in ½ cup all-purpose flour, scraping up all the browned bits, and cook 2 minutes until the roux smells nutty.
Gradually whisk in the stock and the reserved pan juices; bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer and cook 8–10 minutes, whisking often, until the gravy is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Strip the leaves from 2 thyme sprigs.
Stir the thyme leaves in; season with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and ½ teaspoon black pepper, then pour the gravy into a warm gravy boat.
On Thursday: The stuffing is in at 350°F, covered. Bake 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes more until the top is golden and crisp.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
Let the stuffing rest 5 minutes.

On Thursday: peel 5 pounds russet potatoes and cut into 2-inch chunks; put them in a large pot (at least 8-quart), cover with cold salted water by 2 inches, and leave the pot on the stove, off, until it's time to cook.
Turn the burner on under the pot of potatoes and bring to a boil over high heat.
Boil the potatoes over medium-high heat for 18–20 minutes until completely tender when pierced with a fork; drain well and return to the pot.
Warm 1 cup whole milk and ½ cup heavy cream together in a small saucepan or microwave until steaming; mash the drained potatoes with 10 tablespoons butter until smooth.
Stir in the warm milk-cream mixture gradually until the potatoes reach your preferred consistency; season with 2 teaspoons kosher salt and ¼ teaspoon white pepper.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Transfer the potatoes to a warm serving bowl and garnish with 2 tablespoons thinly sliced fresh chives, if using.
On Thursday: The green bean casserole is in at 350°F, covered. Bake 25 minutes.
Uncover, scatter 6 ounces fried onions evenly over the top, and bake uncovered 10 minutes more until the onions are golden and crisp.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
On Thursday: Put the sweet potato casserole in the oven.
The sweet potato casserole is in at 350°F, covered. Bake 20 minutes.
Uncover and bake 10 minutes more until the streusel is golden and the filling is hot — if using marshmallows, broil 1–2 minutes at the very end until toasted.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
On Thursday: whip 1 cup heavy cream to soft peaks and serve alongside the chilled pie, if using.
On Thursday: Remove the turkey from the fridge 1 hour before roasting.
Preheat the oven to 325°F.
Smash 6 cloves garlic and quarter 1 yellow onion.
Rub 6 tablespoons softened butter under the breast skin and over the outside. Stuff the cavity with the 6 cloves garlic, onion quarters, 6 thyme sprigs, 3 rosemary sprigs, and 6 sage leaves.

Scatter 3 celery stalks and 2 carrots (cut into large pieces) and remaining onion pieces in a large roasting pan. Pour in 2 cups broth. Brush the turkey skin with 2 tablespoons neutral oil and set the bird on a roasting rack over the vegetables.
Roast the turkey at 325°F for about 2¼ hours.
Raise the oven to 350°F and put in the Overnight Sage Stuffing and Mashed Potato Casserole.
Keep roasting the turkey at 350°F for about 40 more minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F.
Transfer the turkey to a carving board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 20–30 minutes before carving. Reserve the pan drippings for finishing the gravy.
Carve the turkey and arrange on a large platter to serve.
Serve the Dry-Brined Roast Turkey with the Make-Ahead Turkey Gravy, Overnight Sage Stuffing, Mashed Potato Casserole, Cranberry-Orange Sauce and Green Beans with Crispy Shallots.

On Thursday: Pour the gravy into a medium saucepan. Stir in any pan drippings from the roasted turkey, skimming off excess fat first. Reheat over medium-low heat, stirring, until hot and smooth, about 8 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning with kosher salt and black pepper. Keep warm over the lowest heat, stirring occasionally, until ready to serve.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
On Thursday: The stuffing is in at 350°F, covered. Bake 35 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 minutes more until the top is golden and crisp and the center reads 165°F on an instant-read thermometer.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
On Thursday: The casserole is in at 350°F, covered. Bake 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake 10–15 minutes more until the top is lightly golden and the center is heated through.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
Trim 2½ lb fresh green beans. Thinly slice 4 shallots into rings.
Toss the 4 sliced shallots with 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour in a small bowl until lightly coated. Thinly slice 3 garlic cloves. Zest and juice 1 lemon.

Heat ½ cup neutral oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the floured shallots in a single layer and fry, stirring, until golden and crisp, about 5–6 minutes. Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate and season with a pinch of salt.

Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of oil from the skillet. Add 2 tablespoons butter over medium-high heat. Add the green beans and ½ teaspoon kosher salt and cook, tossing, until bright green and just tender-crisp, about 6 minutes.
Add the 3 cloves sliced garlic and cook, stirring, 1 minute until fragrant. Season with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and ½ teaspoon black pepper. Squeeze the lemon juice over the beans and toss to coat.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Transfer the green beans to a large platter. Scatter the lemon zest and crispy shallots over the top.
On Thursday: Slice the Pumpkin Pie and serve.
On Thursday: Preheat the oven to 400°F.
Scatter the halved onion, 3 roughly chopped celery stalks, and 2 roughly chopped carrots across a large rimmed sheet pan; pour in 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth.
Remove the turkey from the fridge; work the compound butter under the breast skin and rub 3 tablespoons olive oil all over the outside, then squeeze the juice of 2 oranges and 2 lemons over the bird.
Set the turkey skin-side up directly on the vegetables on the sheet pan and roast at 400°F for about 1 hour.
Put the Cornbread and Chorizo Stuffing in the oven with the turkey; the Garlic-Parmesan Smashed Potatoes go in when the turkey comes out.
Keep roasting the turkey at 400°F for about 40 more minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F.
Rest the turkey on the sheet pan, loosely tented with foil, for 20–30 minutes before carving.
Carve the turkey and arrange on a warm platter.

Serve the Citrus-Herb Spatchcock Turkey with the Pan Gravy, Cornbread and Chorizo Stuffing, Garlic-Parmesan Smashed Potatoes, Chipotle-Maple Sweet Potatoes, Cranberry-Jalapeño Relish and Brown-Butter Green Beans.
On Thursday: Pour the turkey drippings from the roasting pan into a fat separator or tall measuring cup; spoon off and reserve ½ cup of the fat, then pour the defatted drippings into the stock.
Heat the reserved ½ cup turkey fat in a medium saucepan over medium; whisk in ½ cup all-purpose flour and cook, stirring constantly, 2 minutes until golden.
Gradually whisk in the warm stock-and-drippings mixture; bring to a boil, then simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until the gravy coats a spoon.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Season with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and ½ teaspoon black pepper; add 2 thyme sprigs and steep 2 minutes, then remove them and pour into a warm gravy boat.
On Thursday: The stuffing is in at 400°F, covered. Bake 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 10–12 more minutes until the top is golden and the center is hot.
Cover the Cornbread and Chorizo Stuffing with foil to keep it warm.
Return the Cornbread and Chorizo Stuffing, uncovered, to the 400°F oven for 10 minutes, until hot again.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
On Thursday: Put 4 lb baby Yukon gold potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water by 2 inches, add 2 tablespoons kosher salt, and leave the pot on the stove, off, until it's time to cook.
Turn the burner on under the pot of potatoes and bring to a boil.
Boil the potatoes 18–20 minutes until completely tender when pierced with a knife; drain well.
Brush two large rimmed sheet pans with some of the ¼ cup olive oil.
Spread the drained potatoes across the two oiled sheet pans; use the bottom of a heavy glass to smash each potato to about ½-inch thick.
Whisk the remaining olive oil, 4 tablespoons melted butter, and 6 minced garlic cloves together; brush generously over every smashed potato.
Put the potatoes in the oven now that the turkey is out.
The potatoes are in at 400°F. Roast 30–35 minutes until the edges are deeply golden and crispy.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.

Immediately scatter 3 oz finely grated Parmesan, the chopped rosemary leaves from 3 sprigs, and ¾ teaspoon black pepper over the hot potatoes; finish with ½ teaspoon flaky sea salt and transfer to a warm platter.
On Thursday: Peel and cut 4 lb sweet potatoes into 1½-inch chunks and place in a large bowl.

Whisk together 3 tablespoons olive oil, 3 tablespoons maple syrup, 2 minced chipotle chiles plus 1 tablespoon adobo sauce, 1 teaspoon cumin, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and ½ teaspoon black pepper; pour over the sweet potatoes and toss to coat; they can sit, covered, in the fridge for a few hours.
Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer across two rimmed sheet pans.
Put the sweet potatoes in the oven.
The sweet potatoes are in at 400°F. Roast 35–40 minutes, flipping once halfway, until caramelized and tender.
Cover the Chipotle-Maple Sweet Potatoes with foil to keep them warm.
Return the Chipotle-Maple Sweet Potatoes, uncovered, to the 400°F oven for 10 minutes, until hot again.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
Transfer the sweet potatoes to a serving platter; squeeze 1 lime over the top and scatter with ½ oz roughly chopped cilantro.
On Thursday: Stir ¼ oz chopped cilantro into the relish just before serving and transfer to a small bowl.
On Thursday: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil; blanch 2½ lb trimmed green beans 3–4 minutes until bright green and just tender, then drain and immediately plunge into a bowl of ice water.
Drain the beans and pat dry; set aside.
Thinly slice 4 garlic cloves and 2 shallots.
Melt 5 tablespoons butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat, swirling often, 4–5 minutes until the foam subsides and the butter turns golden brown and smells nutty.
Add the 4 cloves sliced garlic and 2 thinly sliced shallots to the brown butter and cook, stirring, 2 minutes until softened and fragrant.
Add the blanched green beans, 1 teaspoon kosher salt, and ½ teaspoon black pepper; toss to coat and heat through, 2–3 minutes.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Transfer the green beans to a warm platter; squeeze 1 lemon over the top and scatter with 2 oz toasted sliced almonds.
On Thursday: Lift the bars out using the parchment overhang; cut into 12 bars and serve with whipped cream if desired.

On Thursday: Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Scatter the quartered onion and 2 celery stalks, cut into pieces, in the bottom of a roasting pan; drizzle 1 tablespoon olive oil over the vegetables.
Set the turkey breast skin-side up on the vegetables in the roasting pan and roast at 425°F for 20 minutes to brown the skin.
Reduce the oven to 325°F and continue roasting for about 30 minutes.
Raise the oven to 350°F and put in the Small-Batch Sage Stuffing and Apple Crisp; the Maple-Roasted Sweet Potatoes go in when the turkey breast comes out.
Keep roasting the turkey breast at 350°F for about 30 more minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the breast reads 165°F.
Transfer the turkey breast to a cutting board and rest, tented loosely with foil, for 20 minutes before carving — reserve the drippings in the pan for gravy.
Carve the breast into ½-inch slices and arrange on a warm platter.
Serve the Roast Turkey Breast with the Pan Gravy, Small-Batch Sage Stuffing, Mashed Potatoes, Cranberry-Orange Sauce, Roasted Green Beans and Maple-Roasted Sweet Potatoes.
On Thursday: Open the 32-oz carton of store-bought turkey stock and measure out 2 cups; set aside.
On Thursday: Pour the drippings from the roasting pan into a fat separator or heatproof measuring cup; skim off the fat, reserving ¼ cup fat and ¼ cup drippings.
Place the roasting pan over two burners on medium heat; whisk 3 tablespoons flour into the reserved ¼ cup drippings and cook, whisking constantly, for 2 minutes until golden.
Gradually whisk in the 2 cups turkey stock, scraping up any browned bits; bring to a simmer and cook, whisking often, for 5–7 minutes until the gravy thickens to a pourable consistency.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Season with ½ teaspoon kosher salt and ¼ teaspoon black pepper; pour into a warm gravy boat.
On Thursday: The stuffing is in at 350°F, covered. Bake 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 15 more minutes until the top is golden and crisp.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.

On Thursday: Peel and cut 2 pounds Yukon Gold potatoes into 2-inch chunks; put them in a large saucepan, cover with cold water, add a generous pinch of kosher salt, and leave the pot on the stove, off, until it's time to cook.
Turn the burner on under the pot of potatoes.
Bring the saucepan to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a steady boil and cook the potatoes for 18–20 minutes until completely tender when pierced with a knife.
Drain the potatoes thoroughly, return them to the saucepan, and mash with 4 tablespoons butter until smooth.
Stir in ½ cup warmed whole milk and ¼ cup sour cream; season with 1 teaspoon kosher salt and ¼ teaspoon white pepper.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Transfer the potatoes to a warm serving bowl and garnish with 1 tablespoon sliced fresh chives, if using.
On Thursday: Trim 1 pound green beans.
Toss the green beans in a large bowl with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 thinly sliced garlic cloves, ½ teaspoon kosher salt, and ¼ teaspoon black pepper.
Spread the green beans in a single layer on a large rimmed sheet pan.
Put the green beans in the oven.
The green beans are in at 350°F. Roast 18–20 minutes, tossing once halfway through, until tender and lightly charred at the edges.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
Transfer the green beans to a platter, grate the zest of 1 lemon over the top; scatter 2 tablespoons toasted sliced almonds over the top, if using.
On Thursday: Peel and cut 1½ pounds sweet potatoes into 1-inch cubes; place in a large bowl.

Whisk together 3 tablespoons maple syrup, 2 tablespoons melted butter, ½ teaspoon kosher salt, ¼ teaspoon cinnamon, and ¼ teaspoon black pepper; pour over the sweet potatoes and toss to coat; they can sit, covered, in the fridge for a few hours.
Spread the sweet potatoes in a single layer on a large rimmed sheet pan.
Put the sweet potatoes in the oven now that the turkey breast is out; the green beans go in 15 minutes from now.
The sweet potatoes are in at 350°F. Roast 30–35 minutes, flipping once halfway, until caramelized and tender.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
Transfer the sweet potatoes to a serving dish; scatter 1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves and ¼ teaspoon flaky sea salt over the top, if using.

On Thursday: Peel, core, and slice 3 Granny Smith and 2 Honeycrisp apples ¼-inch thick; toss in a large bowl with the juice of 1 lemon, 3 tablespoons granulated sugar, ½ teaspoon cinnamon, and 1 tablespoon cornstarch.

In a separate bowl, mix ¾ cup rolled oats, ½ cup all-purpose flour, ½ cup packed light brown sugar, ½ teaspoon cinnamon, and ¼ teaspoon kosher salt; work in 6 tablespoons cold cubed butter with your fingers until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs.
Spread the apple mixture evenly into a 9×13-inch baking dish; scatter the oat topping evenly over the apples.
The apple crisp is in at 350°F. Bake 38–42 minutes until the topping is deep golden and the apple juices are bubbling at the edges; cool at least 20 minutes before serving.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
Scoop into bowls and serve warm with vanilla ice cream, if using.
Finely chop the 1½ lb cremini mushrooms, mince the 4 shallots and 6 garlic cloves, and strip 2 tablespoons thyme leaves and chop 1 tablespoon rosemary.

Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high; cook the shallots and garlic 3 minutes, then add the mushrooms, thyme, and rosemary and cook 12–15 minutes, stirring often, until completely dry.

Pour in ¼ cup dry sherry, cook 2 minutes until evaporated, then stir in ½ cup fresh breadcrumbs, ½ cup toasted walnuts, and 2 oz grated vegetarian Parmesan-style cheese; season with ½ teaspoon kosher salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper and let cool.
Open both 7 oz jars of pre-made duxelles and transfer to a bowl; stir in ½ cup toasted walnuts, ½ cup fresh breadcrumbs, and 2 oz grated vegetarian Parmesan-style cheese.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high; sear the 4 portobello caps gill-side down 3 minutes per side, season with ½ teaspoon salt, then cool on a rack.
Wilt the 4 oz baby spinach in the same skillet over medium heat, 2 minutes; transfer to a colander and press out all liquid, then chop roughly.
Preheat the oven to 425°F and line a large rimmed sheet pan with parchment.
Lay one puff pastry sheet on a lightly floured surface; brush the center third with 1½ tablespoons Dijon mustard.
Spread half the duxelles mixture over the mustard zone, top with the spinach and then 2 seared portobello caps; repeat for the second pastry sheet with the remaining filling and caps.
Fold and roll each pastry around its filling, seam-side down on the sheet pan; brush all over with beaten egg and score the tops lightly.
Bake on the sheet pan at 425°F for 25–30 minutes until deep golden brown; rest 5 minutes before slicing into portions.
Slice each Wellington into portions.
Serve the Mushroom Wellington with the Mushroom Gravy, Herb Stuffing, Mashed Potatoes, Balsamic Roasted Brussels Sprouts, Cranberry-Orange Sauce and Baked Mac and Cheese.
Thinly slice 1 lb cremini mushrooms, mince 3 shallots and 4 garlic cloves.
Melt 4 tablespoons butter in a 4-quart saucepan over medium-high; add the 3 shallots and 4 cloves minced garlic and cook 3 minutes until softened.
Add the 1 lb sliced mushrooms and cook 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and their liquid has evaporated.
Sprinkle ⅓ cup flour over the mushrooms and stir 1–2 minutes until the raw flour smell is gone.
Pour in ¼ cup dry sherry and cook 1 minute, then gradually whisk in 4 cups vegetable broth until smooth.
Add 1 tablespoon soy sauce, 1 tablespoon thyme leaves, ¾ teaspoon salt, and ¼ teaspoon pepper; simmer over medium-low 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened to gravy consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning; keep warm over the lowest heat, stirring occasionally, until ready to serve.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
On Thursday: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Bake the stuffing covered at 375°F for 30 minutes.
Uncover and bake 20–25 minutes more until the top is golden and crisp.
Cover the Herb Stuffing with foil to keep it warm while the oven heats for the next dish.
Return the Herb Stuffing, uncovered, to the 425°F oven for 10 minutes, until hot again.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
Thinly slice 2 tbsp fresh chives; keep it covered in a small container in the fridge until serving.

Peel and cut 5 lb russet potatoes into 2-inch chunks; put them in a large pot with the 4 peeled garlic cloves, cover with cold salted water, and leave the pot on the stove, off, until it's time to cook.
Turn the burner on under the pot of potatoes.
Bring the pot to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a vigorous simmer and cook 18–20 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender when pierced.
Warm 1 cup whole milk in a small saucepan over low heat until steaming; keep warm.
Drain the potatoes and garlic, return to the pot, and let steam dry 2 minutes over low heat.
Mash the potatoes and garlic with 8 tablespoons butter until smooth, then stir in the warm milk, ½ cup sour cream, 1½ teaspoons salt, and ¼ teaspoon white pepper.
Cover and keep warm over the lowest heat.
Transfer the potatoes to a serving bowl and garnish with the chives you sliced this morning.
Preheat the oven to 425°F.
Trim and halve 3 lb Brussels sprouts.
Whisk together ¼ cup olive oil, 3 tablespoons balsamic vinegar, 1½ tablespoons honey, 4 minced garlic cloves, 1 teaspoon salt, and ½ teaspoon pepper in a large bowl.
Toss the Brussels sprouts in the balsamic mixture and spread cut-side down in a single layer across two large rimmed sheet pans.
Roast at 425°F for 22–25 minutes, rotating the pans halfway through, until the sprouts are deeply caramelized and tender.
Cover the Balsamic Roasted Brussels Sprouts with foil to keep them warm.
Return the Balsamic Roasted Brussels Sprouts, uncovered, to the 425°F oven for 10 minutes, until hot again.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
Transfer the Brussels sprouts to a serving platter, scatter with ¼ cup dried cranberries, and top with 3 tablespoons toasted pine nuts if using.
On Thursday: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
On Thursday: Toss 1 cup panko breadcrumbs with 2 tablespoons melted butter and the remaining 4 oz sharp cheddar; scatter evenly over the cold mac and cheese.
Bake uncovered at 375°F for 45–50 minutes until the crumb topping is deep golden and the edges are bubbling.
Cover the Baked Mac and Cheese with foil to keep it warm.
Return the Baked Mac and Cheese, uncovered, to the 425°F oven for 10 minutes, until hot again.
Turn the oven off and leave the sides inside, covered loosely with foil, to keep warm.
Take the sides out of the oven.
Let the mac and cheese rest 5 minutes.
On Thursday: Slice the Apple Pie and serve.
